groups.notes: Ten eligible units, all integrated, all started at ladder index 0 - the only step this repository has ever measured. Recommendation retained unchanged. Group confidence is low despite n=10 because the sample is single-armed: costToAcceptance can rank units against each other but cannot rank steps against each other, which is what a start recommendation requires. Three of ten were accepted on the first review with no fix pass; seven required at least one fix pass and re-review. That re-review rate is a hint that a stronger start might be cheaper, but the rubric's floor-raise grounds are not met: no capability failure was recorded on any unit, and no stronger step was ever run, so the required 25%-lower-median comparison cannot be computed. No floor lowering is possible either - index 0 is the lowest verified step - and for the same reason no boundary probe is schedulable below it. CONFOUND, stated explicitly rather than controlled: costToAcceptance here is driven jointly by attempt count and by context size, and the two are not separable in this telemetry. Issue #50 (large group) is the clearest illustration - accepted on the first review with zero findings and still the second most expensive unit in the run at $17.75 - and the same effect is present inside this group (#59 cost $24.32 across 3 attempts on a 1235-line single-file change, while #49 cost $7.30 across 3 attempts on a 187-line change). Any future ranking of steps by median costToAcceptance in this group must normalise for change size or it will attribute context cost to route quality. capabilityEscalation is recorded as 0 because the telemetry records no capability failure or route change on any attempt; it is not evidence that escalation was tried and unnecessary. Issue #111 added (feature-reviewed, evidenceStage feature-reviewed): accepted at ladder index 0 with one cosmetic standards fix pass, consistent with this group's existing re-review rate. Its two failed planner attempts (API 529 overload) and its one failed reviewer attempt (sandbox had no network, could not allocate review children) all carry capabilityFailure:false in the source telemetry and are excluded from capability learning per the calibration rubric; they are ordinary infrastructure retries, not evidence for or against this route. #111 reported no usage/cost/duration (all null), so it is counted in samples but not folded into the dollar-based costToAcceptance median above, which still reflects only the prior nine cost-reporting units. No floor change: still a single additional non-capability-clean unit, short of the two-unit raise threshold, and index 0 remains the lowest verified step.

groups.notes: Four eligible units, all integrated at ladder index 0. Recommendation retained unchanged; three units cannot carry a per-size threshold and, as with the other groups, no stronger step was ever run so no comparison is available. #50 and #57 were accepted on their first review with no fix pass (#57's second session is a merger, not a fix pass); #58 required one fix pass. CONFOUND: this group is where the cost/context confound is most visible. #50 is the second most expensive unit in the entire run at $17.75 despite one attempt and one clean review, purely because its context was large - a grouping that reads costToAcceptance as a proxy for route quality would rank #50's step as poor when the step in fact landed it first time. The median recorded here ($13.09) should therefore not be compared against another group's median or against a future step's median without normalising for change size. capabilityEscalation is recorded as 0 because the telemetry records no capability failure or route change on any attempt; it is not evidence that escalation was tried and unnecessary. Issue #113 added (feature-reviewed): accepted at ladder index 0 with zero review findings on the first independent round (execute_reviewed_plan cut from 298 to 40 lines). Two planner attempts failed on API 529 overload and one implementer attempt died with a harness 'Execution error' (exit 144) before doing any work; all three carry capabilityFailure:false in the source telemetry and are excluded from capability learning as ordinary infrastructure/harness retries, not implementer capability evidence. #113 reported no usage/cost/duration (all null), so it is counted in samples but not folded into the dollar-based costToAcceptance median above, which still reflects only the prior three cost-reporting units. No floor change: the unit succeeded cleanly at the existing floor, which is consistent with (not sufficient to lower further, since index 0 is already the lowest verified step) the current recommendation.
